name: Tennessee Veer N Shoot
subtitle: Tennessee Volunteers · CFB 27
tagline: Find the numbers. Take the shot.

about.headline: WHO ARE THE VOLS
copy: Josh Heupel quarterbacked Oklahoma to the 2000 national title, and he picked this offense up as the coordinator at Missouri in 2016, the first time the Briles system showed up in the SEC. He took it to UCF, went 12-1 in his first season, and landed in Knoxville in January 2021 at a program that had not won ten games since 2007.

In 2022 it all hit. Tennessee went {rec|11-2}, led the country in scoring at {ppg|46.1 points a game} and in total offense at 525.5 yards a game, beat Alabama {bama|52-49} on a field goal as time expired, and sat at number one in the first playoff rankings. Hendon Hooker threw 27 touchdowns against two interceptions, and Jalin Hyatt won the Biletnikoff with 15 touchdown catches, five of them against Alabama.

Heupel won 45 games in his first five seasons, with an Orange Bowl, a Citrus Bowl and a playoff trip in 2024. He did it with receivers split wider than anybody in the country, a handful of looks with a play stacked on top of every one, and shots down the field that were never a gamble. That is the offense we are building, out of the Auburn playbook in College Football 27.

principles.title: FIND THE NUMBERS ADVANTAGE
principles.blurb: Before every snap, find where we have more than they do, in the run game or the pass game, and attack it.
principles.detail: Every play starts with a count: where do we have more than they do. A light box is a run, a loaded box is a throw to the perimeter, and a defender who leaves his spot has given you the numbers behind him. In the game it is the first thing you do at the line, in the run game and the pass game both.

pages.title: Where do we have more than they do
pages.text: Every play in this offense starts with the same question: where is our numbers advantage? It is not a run thing or a pass thing. If they leave the box light, we run it. If they load the box, they are short on the perimeter and we throw it out there. If a defender leaves his spot to chase something, we throw it into the spot he left. We are not guessing what they are in. We are counting, and attacking where they are short.
points: Count the box, count the perimeter, take the side where you have more
A light box is a run, a loaded box is a throw to the outside
A defender who leaves his spot just gave you the numbers behind him

pages.title: The count is built into the call
pages.text: Heupel builds the count into the play. A lot of the Tennessee offense is a run with a throw attached, so the quarterback never has to be wrong: hand it off when the box is light, throw it when a defender comes down to even things up. In 2022 it led the country in scoring at 46.1 points a game, with Jaylen Wright and Jabari Small running for 23 touchdowns between them into boxes that could not load up.
points: A run with a throw attached, so the count decides the play
46.1 points a game, first in the country
Two backs, 23 rushing touchdowns, against boxes that could not load up

pages.title: RPO Alert Post Iso, Stack HB Screen, the swing
pages.text: On RPO Alert Post Iso you count the box: both safeties back means six in the box against our seven, so hand it off, and when the overhang cheats down the skinny post is behind him. On Stack HB Screen you count the stack: three on two, throw it every time, and three on three means the box is empty and the quarterback runs. On the swing series the user leaves the middle to chase the back, and the cross comes into the spot he left.
points: Six in the box against seven is a handoff
Three on two over the stack is a screen every time
QB Blast is six on four when they stay spread out

principles.title: USE THE WHOLE FIELD
principles.blurb: Split them out past the numbers and the defense has to cover every inch of the width, which leaves open grass for the run and the pass.
principles.detail: Heupel splits his receivers wider than anybody in college football, because every defender who walks out to cover them is one who cannot help in the box or in the middle of the field. That width is where the open grass comes from: the seams, the tight end up the middle, the light box for the run. In the game the splits also make the defense show you what it is in before the snap.

pages.title: Make them cover the whole width
pages.text: The wide splits are where the open grass comes from. When the receivers line up out past the numbers, the defense has to go out there with them, and every defender who walks out is one who cannot help in the box or in the middle of the field. The corners are too far away to help inside, the safeties have to split the whole field, and the linebackers are left covering a huge area on their own. That space is what we run into and throw into.
points: Every defender who walks out to the numbers is one fewer in the box
The seams and the middle of the field open up for the pass
The defense has to show you what it is in before the snap

pages.title: Wider than anybody in the country
pages.text: Nobody spreads the field like Heupel. Tennessee lines its receivers up outside the numbers, close to the sideline, and uses nearly all 53 yards of width on every snap. He points to spacing as the thing that makes his offense different. The splits make the secondary declare its coverage before the snap, and in 2022 that spacing was worth 525.5 yards a game, the most in the country.
points: Receivers outside the numbers, close to the sideline
The secondary has to declare its coverage before the snap
525.5 yards a game in 2022, first in the country

pages.title: The seam, the tight end, the light box
pages.text: You see it on every call. On All Go the safety cannot get over to the seam, because the split starts him too far away. On X Replace and PA Y Pop the tight end is a cheat code up the middle, because the linebackers have nobody to help them. And in the run game the stack and five wide pull defenders out of the box, so ISO Y Insert, the counter and the quarterback runs are all hitting a light box.
points: Single high and the seam is open, the safety is too far away
The tight end owns the middle of the field
The stack pulls three defenders out of the box by itself

principles.title: CREATE EXPLOSIVE PASS PLAYS
principles.blurb: Once they are spread out and worried about the numbers, the shot is there, and the choice routes send it where the safeties are not.
principles.detail: Once the numbers have pulled a safety down and the splits are holding the corners outside, the deep ball is the open throw, not a gamble. The choice routes read the safeties after the snap and go where they are not: the post when the middle is open, the dig or the seam when it is closed. In the game you read the same thing the receiver reads, so you never have to force it.

pages.title: Make them pay over the top
pages.text: Everything else sets this up. The numbers pull a safety down into the box, the splits hold the corners outside, and now the deep ball is not a gamble, it is the open throw. The choice routes finish it: the receiver reads the safeties after the snap and runs to where they are not, the post when the middle of the field is open, the dig or the seam when it is closed. We are not hoping the shot is there. We are reading whether it is.
points: The run game and the screens are what earn the shot
Middle of the field open is a post, closed is a dig or a seam
The play fakes look exactly like the runs they just saw

pages.title: Thirty six plays of forty yards or more
pages.text: The 2022 Volunteers had 36 plays of 40 yards or more, eight clear of the next team in the country and the most by anybody since 2017. Hendon Hooker threw 27 touchdowns against two interceptions, and Jalin Hyatt caught 15 of them out of the slot, five in one afternoon against Alabama. They were not forcing it down the field. The ball went deep because the offense kept leaving somebody open deep.
points: 36 plays of 40 yards or more, first in the country
27 touchdowns to 2 interceptions for Hooker
Hyatt: 15 touchdown catches, five against Alabama

pages.title: Choice Deep Drag, Slot Choice Smash, PA Y Pop, PA Wheel
pages.text: Choice Deep Drag and Slot Choice Smash are the choice routes: a dig against one high, a post against two, a seam against Cover 3, with a wheel and a second seam layered around them. PA Y Pop and PA Wheel are the shots off the run game, the same backfield picture as the counter and the iso with a seam or a corner behind the linebackers. And when the corner starts coming up on the swing, MTN Double Pass goes over his head.
points: Read the safeties first: one high or two
The motioned seam on PA Y Pop is open almost every time
Stack Fk Screen Cross: the screen look with a cross and a post behind it

playbook.title: RUN THE AUBURN PLAYBOOK
playbook.note: In College Football 27 this whole offense runs out of the AUBURN playbook, the same book as every Veer N Shoot install. All four Wide formations and every call on the sheet live inside it.

about.front: art/Veer N Shoot Offense__Tenn Stadium Outside.webp

jobs: COUNT THE PERIMETER AND THE BOX BEFORE EVERY SNAP.
THROW THE SCREEN OR THE BUBBLE WHEN WE HAVE NUMBERS OUTSIDE.
TUCK IT ON THE DRAW WHEN THEY WALK OUT OF THE BOX.
THROW THE CHOICE ROUTE WHERE THE SAFETIES ARE NOT.
WORK THE SWING SERIES: THE SWING, THE CORNER, THE SLANT, THE RUN.
RUN THE STREAK THAT HOLDS THE CORNER AND THE SAFETY OUTSIDE.
RUN THE CHOICE: THE DIG AGAINST ONE HIGH, THE POST AGAINST TWO.
WIN THE POST AND THE POST SIT ON THE BACKSIDE.
BLOCK THE PERIMETER ON THE SCREEN AND THE BUBBLE.
RUN THE SLOT OPTION: SIT, SEAM, DIG OR POST.
WIN THE SEAM AGAINST SINGLE HIGH.
BREAK THE OPTION ROUTE OUTSIDE AGAINST MAN ON SHOCK.
RUN THE CORNER BEHIND THE SWING.
MOTION ACROSS AND RUN THE SEAM ON PA Y POP.
MOTION OUT AND RUN THE CORNER ON PA WHEEL.
LEAD THE ISO THROUGH THE HOLE.
RUN THE CROSS OFF THE FAKE SCREEN AND THE SEAM ON X REPLACE.
HIT THE ISO DOWNHILL WITH NO WASTED MOVEMENT.
FOLLOW THE PULLER ON THE COUNTER.
RUN THE SWING MOTION ON EVERY PLAY IN THE SERIES.
CATCH THE SCREEN BEHIND THE STACK.

player.name: HENDON HOOKER
player.line: Twenty seven touchdowns, two interceptions. The quarterback of the best offense in the country.
player.bio: Transferred in from Virginia Tech in 2021 and became the perfect quarterback for this offense. In 2022 he threw for 3,135 yards and 27 touchdowns against two interceptions, completed 69.6 percent, ran for 430 more, and beat Alabama {bama|52-49} with five touchdown passes. He was the SEC Offensive Player of the Year and finished fifth in the Heisman voting, the first Volunteer in the top five since Peyton Manning, before a knee injury in November ended his season. The Lions took him in the third round.
goodAt: Deep accuracy on the choice routes.
Enough legs to make the box count matter.
roleFor: The quarterback in this offense is a counter before he is a thrower. Before every snap he counts the defenders over the stack or the trips and the defenders left in the box, and that count tells him whether it is the screen, the bubble or a quarterback run. On the swing series he watches who chases the back and throws behind him.

On the choice routes he reads the same thing the receiver reads: a safety in the middle of the field means the dig, no safety means the post. Deep accuracy is the one thing this role cannot live without, and the legs are what make the defense pay for walking out of the box.
player.oneLine: Count it, throw it where the safeties are not, and run when they leave the box.

lineage.name: HENDON HOOKER
stats: SEC Offensive Player of the Year
lineage.brought: The deep ball and the legs to make the box count matter. He threw it where the safeties were not and almost never threw it to the other team.

player.name: CEDRIC TILLMAN
player.line: The big outside receiver. A thousand yards the year before, and the man the corners had to stay on.
player.bio: The outside receiver in Heupel's first two seasons. In 2021 he caught 64 balls for 1,081 yards and 12 touchdowns, and in 2022 an ankle injury held him to six games, where he still caught 37 passes for 417 yards. At six foot three he was the one who won on the outside while the splits pulled everybody else apart. He went in the third round of the 2023 draft.
goodAt: Holds the corner and the safety with the streak.
Runs the post and the post sit.
roleFor: The outside receiver lines up out past the numbers, and the streak he runs on most snaps is what makes the rest of the offense work: it holds the corner and it holds the safety, which is why the seam and the crosser inside of him are open.

On Choice Deep Drag he is the choice route itself, the dig against one high and the post against two. On the screens and the bubble he is a blocker on the perimeter, and those blocks are the difference between five yards and fifty.
player.oneLine: Hold the corner outside, run the choice, and block the perimeter.

lineage.name: CEDRIC TILLMAN
lineage.brought: The big body outside the numbers. The streak that holds the corner and the safety, and the choice route behind it.

player.name: JALIN HYATT
player.line: The Biletnikoff winner. Five touchdowns against Alabama out of the slot.
player.bio: The breakout star of 2022. Lined up in the slot, where nobody could run with him, he caught 67 passes for 1,267 yards and a school record 15 touchdowns, and he scored five times in the {bama|52-49} win over Alabama on six catches for 207 yards. He won the Biletnikoff Award, the first in Tennessee history, was a unanimous All-American, and went to the Giants in the third round.
goodAt: Speed nobody in the slot can match.
Wins the seam and the post.
Reads the safety on the option route.
roleFor: The slot receiver is who the choice routes are built for. On Slot Choice Smash and Deep Choice Drag he reads the coverage after the snap: he sits against zone, throws his route up the seam against Cover 3, and turns it into a post or a dig against two high.

The wide splits mean there is no help for whoever is covering him, so against single high the seam is open and against man the option route breaks away from the defender. Speed and a clean release are what the role needs.
player.oneLine: Read the safeties and finish with the route they cannot cover.

lineage.name: JALIN HYATT
lineage.brought: The fastest man on the field in the slot. The option route and the seam that nobody could run with.

player.name: PRINCETON FANT
player.line: The H-back who did everything. Nine touchdowns three different ways.
player.bio: The movable piece in the 2022 offense. He caught 22 passes for 241 yards and three touchdowns, ran for five more out of short yardage packages, and threw one, nine touchdowns in all. Heupel lined him up as a tight end, an H-back and a fullback, and moved him across the formation before the snap to change the picture.
goodAt: Leads the back through the hole.
Runs the seam behind a play fake.
roleFor: The H-back is what makes one look into several plays. He leads the iso, he is the lead blocker on the quarterback power, and then on the play action that looks just like those runs he is the one running free.

On PA Y Pop he motions across and runs the seam behind the linebackers who stepped up. On PA Wheel he motions out to make trips and runs the corner. On X Replace and the fake screen he is the seam and the cross in the middle of the field that the splits leave empty.
player.oneLine: Block it like a run, then run right past them on the fake.

lineage.name: PRINCETON FANT
stats: Nine total touchdowns: five rushing, three receiving, one passing
lineage.brought: The movable piece. He leads the iso, motions across for the seam and motions out for the corner.

player.name: JAYLEN WRIGHT
player.line: The home run back. Six yards a carry behind a box that could not load up.
player.bio: Led the 2022 team in rushing as a sophomore with 875 yards and ten touchdowns on 146 carries, six yards a carry, splitting the work with Jabari Small. With the receivers split that wide, the box was light every week, and he was fast enough to turn a crease into a touchdown.
roleFor: The running back gets a light box on almost every snap, so his runs are downhill and simple: the iso on his own side with the tight end, and the counter behind the pulling guard when they sit in two high.

His other job is the swing. He motions out to the wide side on every play in the swing series, and whether he gets the ball or not, the defender who chases him is the one the quarterback throws behind.
player.oneLine: Get downhill into the light box, and make them chase the swing.

lineage.name: JAYLEN WRIGHT
lineage.brought: The downhill back. The iso, the counter, and the swing motion that the whole series is built on.

formations.name: Wide 5WR
formations.desc: Empty, with three receivers to one side and two to the other, all of them split out wide. This is where the choice routes live, and where the defense has to pick: walk out and leave the box to the quarterback, or stay in and give up the bubble.
bullets: Count the defenders over the trips before every snap
The slot option route is right against every coverage
The quarterback runs into whatever box they leave

formations.name: Wide Doubles Y Off Stack
formations.desc: Three stacked on top of each other out on the numbers, with the tight end off the line on the other side. The screen, the run and the shot all come out of the exact same picture, and the stack pulls three defenders out of the box to cover it.
bullets: Three on two over the stack is a screen every time
Three on three means the box is empty
The tight end owns the middle of the field
formations.img: art/Tennessee__Wide Doubles Y Off Stack Formation.svg

formations.name: Wide Slot Right Wk
formations.desc: Two receivers and the H-back to one side, the back set away from them. The swing series lives here: the back motions out to the wide side on every play, and what happens behind him is different every time.
bullets: The same swing motion on four different plays
The counter gets four blockers on three to the tight end side
The motioned seam is open behind the play fake

formations.name: Wide Slot Right
formations.desc: The same look with the back on the strong side, behind the H-back. Two calls: the iso with the alert post built in, and the play action that looks exactly like it.
bullets: The iso and the play action are the same picture
Motion the H-back out and it becomes trips

pillars.name: Base Offense
pillars.eyebrow: the base plays and their twins
pillars.line: Where every game starts. This section is about making the defense defend the whole width of the field before it gets to defend anything else: a run and a screen that punish them for how they line up, and a shot that comes off the exact same picture once they start cheating to stop it. The goal is to get comfortable counting numbers at the line, and to learn that every base play here has a twin.

checks: Both safeties are back and the iso has the numbers in the box
The overhang cheats on the run and the skinny post is behind him
They jump the screen and the cross is behind them

pillars.name: Veer N Shoot Essentials
pillars.line: The choice routes are what make it a veer and shoot. The receiver does not run a set path: he reads the safeties after the snap and finishes with the route they cannot cover, so one call has an answer for one high, two high and match. This section is about learning to read the same picture he reads, out of five wide, where the splits make that picture easy to see.

checks: One high, the choice is a dig in front of the safety
Two high, it is a post that splits them
The wheel, the seam and the drag are layered off the same routes

pillars.name: Swing Series
pillars.line: One motion, four plays. The back swings to the wide side on every snap in this section, and what happens behind him changes every time: a quarterback run, a throw behind the defender who chased him, a trick. This section is about making the defense wrong for reacting, so by the fourth time they see the swing they do not know whether to chase it or stay home.

checks: They get caught inside and the swing has two blockers in front of it
The user leaves the middle to take it and the quarterback runs power
He keeps leaving and the cross, the dig and the streak are behind him

pillars.name: Scheme Kings
pillars.line: The rest of the offense out of the same four formations, exclusive to Scheme Kings with a breakdown on every one: the bubble RPO and the blast out of five wide, the quick snap verticals, the man beater, the third choice route, the quarterback run and the iso out of the stack, the mesh with the tight end seam, the counter and the play action that comes off it.

checks: RPO Bubble QB Draw when they stay tight, QB Blast when they spread out
PA Y Pop: the motioned seam behind the counter fake
Shock: the option route, and the stack against press man

home.pitch: Receivers split wider than anybody, a swing series and a stack where every play has a twin, and choice routes that make the deep shot the safe throw. All of it out of the Auburn playbook.

book.note: every formation and every call on the sheet lives inside it

plays.name: RPO Alert Post Iso

reads.label: Read the Overhang
reads.text: Keep your eyes on the overhang defender over the skinny post on the wide side, or whoever is over the slot if he is inside. At the snap, if he stays on the slot or backpedals, hand the ball off.

reads.label: The Iso
reads.text: A really nice downhill run. The tight end leads through the hole, the line gets to the second level, and there is a cutback to the outside when you need it. Third and three, and it gets explosive.

reads.label: Count the Box
reads.text: This is the play for when both safeties are back and they are matching the spread outside. That leaves six in the box against five linemen, a sixth blocker and the back, so you outnumber them. It is a well blocked play anyway, and with the numbers it went for thirteen.

reads.label: The Skinny Post
reads.text: What makes the play so good. If the overhang jumps down, jumps inside, or jumps outside, anything except playing back over the top of it, throw the skinny post in behind their heads. Even with a safety coming over the top he is too late: throw it inside of him as the post breaks in. Two walk in touchdowns.

reads.label: The Backside Slant
reads.text: If you do not think the post will be there but you like the look on the backside better, read that side the same way. Everybody bites down, the corner plays off, and there is a hole for the slant. Throw it instead of handing it off, for thirteen.

adjustments: Two receiver side and the H-back to the wide side of the field
Backside solo receiver on a slant
plays.whenToUse: One of the favorite plays in the scheme, and one you call an absolute ton. Find the numbers advantage in the box and hand it off, and the moment the overhang cheats on the run, the skinny post is behind him. PA Wheel is the same backfield picture.

plays.name: PA Wheel

reads.label: The Corner Against Zone
reads.text: The play fake looks just like the iso. Against zone the streak runs the deep defender off, and if the flat defender comes inside or bites down, throw the corner route as it gets up over the top of him.

reads.label: The Corner Against Man
reads.text: Leave the outside receiver on his post and it is one on one for the motioned H-back on the corner. He breaks outside with two or three yards of separation. That turned third and twenty three into fourth and two.

reads.label: The Slot Post
reads.text: The next place to look, man or zone. Against man he cuts across in front of the safety. Against zone, when the flat gets back, the user leaves to help on the corner or the linebackers bite on the cross, he breaks in behind them.

reads.label: The Outside Post
reads.text: Against man there are four good routes on the field: the corner, both posts and the shallow cross. The outside post behind the slot went for a touchdown.

reads.label: The Shallow Cross
reads.text: The solo receiver comes underneath everything. Against zone he is the checkdown under the flat defender who sank on the corner. Against man he runs away from his defender for four or five yards of separation.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Motion the H-back out to make trips, then put him on a corner route
Zone, or you are not sure: outside receiver on the trips side on a streak
Man: leave the outside receiver on his post
plays.whenToUse: One of the go to plays in the scheme. If you think it is zone or you do not know, put the outside man on the streak and throw the corner. If you know it is man, leave him on the post and you have four man beaters.

plays.name: Stack HB Screen

reads.label: Count the Stack Side
reads.text: Before the snap, count the defenders over the stack. We have two blockers and the receiver. If they have two out there, it is three on two and you throw it every single time. Get it out right away.

reads.label: Even Numbers, Tuck It
reads.text: Three defenders over the stack and you are probably not throwing it, unless they all bust inside at the snap. But they had to leave the box to get out there, so tuck it and run. It is not a scramble, treat it as a designed quarterback draw.

reads.label: The Tight End in the Flat
reads.text: The other side is a slant flat combination. If the linebacker has to come all the way out to take the tight end in the flat, he is in a tough spot. Quick throw it for nine.

reads.label: The Slant Behind Him
reads.text: The slant comes in over the top of the flat route. If the linebacker runs out with the tight end, it is right behind him.

adjustments: Stack to the short side of the field, so the screen goes to the short side
plays.whenToUse: A numbers play. Three on two outside, throw the screen. Three on three, the box is empty and the quarterback runs. Stack Fk Screen Cross and Stack QB Zone look exactly like it.

plays.name: Stack Fk Screen Cross

reads.label: The Tight End Cross
reads.text: Run it like Y Cross. With these splits the defense has to widen out so far that one user is trying to cover the whole middle of the field. Throw the tight end early if there is an opening right away, or wait until he clears the linebackers and the flat defender stays shallow.

reads.label: The Skinny Post Alert
reads.text: The streak runs the deep defender off and the skinny post breaks in behind it. Against Cover 2 with no deep middle dropper it is wide open between the safeties. Against Cover 4 match, look for a safety caught in trail coming out of the stack and take the shot.

reads.label: The Post Sit
reads.text: If the tight end is taken away in the middle, come to the backside. When the flat defender stays shallow and the deep defender plays off, the post sit settles right between the two.

reads.label: The Back on the Drag
reads.text: The checkdown. Quick pressure, get it out to him. Or everybody plays back, he comes all the way across the field and you drop it down.

adjustments: Stack to the wide side of the field
Running back in the stack on a drag (or the shallow in cut)
Outside receiver on the short side on a post sit
plays.whenToUse: The shot off the stack. They have seen the screen out of this look, and now the tight end is crossing behind them with a post over the top. Cross, post sit, checkdown, with the skinny post as the alert.

plays.name: Choice Deep Drag

reads.label: The Wheel
reads.text: It does not really matter what the coverage is. Against Cover 2 or Cover 3 the motioned streak pulls the deep defender back, the flat defender settles, and the slot wheels up the sideline into the pocket between them. Cover 2 or Cover 3 only changes how big that pocket is.

reads.label: The Choice Against One High
reads.text: The outside receiver has two options, a dig or a post. There is a safety in the post, so he runs the dig in front of him. With the drag underneath you are high lowing the linebackers, and stemming him up one notch means they never get deep enough.

reads.label: The Choice Against Two High
reads.text: Two safeties and the middle of the field is open, so he turns it into a post. If they have no deep middle dropper, the streak has run one safety off and he splits the two of them. Fire it over the top.

reads.label: The Motioned Streak
reads.text: The option routes put a lot of stress on the defense. If you see match, Cover 2, or any confusion and the middle of the field is open, pass lead the streak up and inside for the touchdown.

reads.label: The Drag
reads.text: Everybody playing way back, no wheel, no post, no dig. Check it down to the drag underneath.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Middle slot receiver on the wide side on a streak, then motion him across
Outside receiver on the short side: stem his route up one notch
Inside slot on the trips side stays on his drag (put him on one if he is not)
plays.whenToUse: The essential choice route. Dig if there is a safety in the middle, post if there is not, and the wheel, the streak and the drag layered around it. Call it when you want a shot and you are not sure what they are in.

plays.name: Slot Choice Smash

reads.label: The Seam Against Cover 3
reads.text: Key off the slot option. Against Cover 3 he would hitch up, but stemming him up one notch lets you throw it as a seam. Jammed or free release, as soon as he clears the flat defender, let it go.

reads.label: The Post Against Two High
reads.text: Two safeties high and he turns it into a post, with the dig underneath him. Cover 2 with no deep middle dropper, bomb it. Cover 4 and the match defender gets caught sitting on the dig, bomb it.

reads.label: The Seam on the Other Side
reads.text: Against Cover 3 there is a second seam from the slot on the two receiver side. If the middle safety overshoots to the trips, wait until he clears and hit the backside seam.

reads.label: The Dig Against Match
reads.text: Overload match with verticals and it has problems. Three go vertical on one side for so long before the dig cuts that the match defenders have to change who they have late. The quarter flat got toasted by twenty yards, and the next time it was the safety caught flat footed.

reads.label: The Drag Underneath
reads.text: Against zone, when the option and the seam are not there, high low the linebackers. They bite down on the drag, throw the dig over their heads. They all stay back, throw the drag.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Outside receiver on the wide side on a streak
Slot receiver on the short side on a streak
Outside receiver on the short side on a drag
Middle slot on the option route: stem him up one notch
plays.whenToUse: The second essential. The slot option is a seam against Cover 3 and a post against two high, there is a seam on both sides, and the dig behind three verticals is one of the best answers to match coverage in the game.

plays.name: MTN RPO QB Power

reads.label: The Swing
reads.text: Snap it and the back auto motions out on the swing with two blockers in front of him. If the defenders get caught inside, or there are only two of them out there, fire it out to him. Rack catch and go. That one was fifteen yards down inside the five.

reads.label: The QB Power
reads.text: This is what makes it so good, and the timing on it is perfect. Throw the swing a few times and the user gets super aggressive, leaving the middle of the field to take it. Now hold the ball. The guards pull across, there are blockers out in front, the user is out of position, and you tuck it, put your foot in the ground and run power.

reads.label: The Backside Slant
reads.text: The third option. The linebackers shoot down hard and there is an extra defender out on the swing, so it is not open. The slant from the backside comes into the middle of the field and replaces the linebackers who left.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field, so the swing goes to the wide side
Outside receiver on the short side on a slant
plays.whenToUse: The first play of the swing series and the one that sets up everything else. Simple but very effective: throw the swing until the user starts leaving the middle to take it, then hold it and run power behind the pullers.

plays.name: MTN Double Pass

reads.label: Run the Power First
reads.text: The next layer of the swing series. Run MTN RPO QB Power once or twice first, so everybody gets aggressive coming downhill on the swing. Then call this.

reads.label: The Streak Over the Top
reads.text: Throw the swing out, then keep your eye on the defender over the outside receiver. If he stops his feet to come down, it is one on one with a step. Be patient, set your feet, let the receiver actually run, and throw it over the top.

reads.label: He Does Not Bite, Take Off
reads.text: If that defender is all over the streak, do not try to throw it. You are already out on the swing with the back, so just take off. The two receivers turn into blockers down the field, and that went for thirty five.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field, so the swing goes to the wide side
plays.whenToUse: A really good trick play you can use about once a game, after the swing has them flying downhill. Sometimes it draws an illegal blocking downfield flag, so do not live in it.

plays.name: MTN Slot Cross

reads.label: The Slot Cross
reads.text: Run the QB power a few times first, because you want the linebacker super aggressive on the swing. He leaves the middle of the field and the slot cross comes right into the spot he vacated. Hit it early into that hole if you have time, or wait for him to come all the way across and throw it late.

reads.label: The Dig Behind It
reads.text: If the crosser is not there, the dig is coming in behind it. Throw it right away as he breaks, or wait a little longer and let it really break in behind the crosser.

reads.label: The H-Back Option
reads.text: Stock he is on a check and release hook, but the option route might be a little better. Against zone he sits down. Against man he breaks inside or outside, and on third and ten he broke inside and we dropped it in.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field, so the swing goes to the wide side
Solo receiver on the short side on a streak
Optional: H-back on an option route instead of the check and release hook
plays.whenToUse: The pass off the swing, and the reason these plays are packaged together. Once the user is leaving the middle to take the swing, the cross and the dig are coming into the spot he just left.

plays.name: MTN RPO QB Draw

reads.label: Tuck It and Run
reads.text: It is a pass play with a quarterback draw built in. If you do not like the look of the pass, put your foot in the ground and run. It is designed for that, not a scramble. Ten yards in the open field, and a walk in on the goal line.

reads.label: The Corner Early
reads.text: The swing leaves the backfield and you want them reacting to it. When the defender jumps down on the swing, throw the corner early as the slot breaks up the field.

reads.label: The Corner Late
reads.text: Or wait. Everybody comes down on the swing, he breaks to the outside, and you throw the corner behind all of them.

reads.label: The Backside Slant
reads.text: If everybody bites on the swing and the corner is not open, the slant is coming from the solo side. Fourth and three, drop it in, break a tackle, house call.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field, so the swing goes to the wide side
Slot receiver on the wide side on a C corner route: inside release, up, then out
Backside solo receiver on a slant
plays.whenToUse: The last play in the swing series. By now they are chasing the swing, so the corner breaks behind them, the slant comes in from the backside, and if none of it is there the quarterback run is built in.

plays.name: RPO Bubble QB Draw

reads.label: Count the Trips Side
reads.text: Look to the trips side where the bubble is and count the defenders over our receivers. If there are three out there, check the backside for two. If they are staying wide on both sides, you are probably keeping it.

reads.label: The Draw
reads.text: Two safeties back and everybody spaced out wide is the perfect time to run it. It is technically a pass, so anyone in a pass fit drops back, and you take off for an easy fifteen. Make the safety miss in the hole and it is a touchdown.

reads.label: The Bubble
reads.text: Throw it one of two times: they only have two over the three, or the inside defender over the bubble jumps inside at the snap. Two blockers out in front, rack catch, get up the field. That one went for fifty.

reads.label: The Backside Hitches
reads.text: Same idea on the other side. If the defenders over the two hitches jump inside, or you thought you were running and at the last second the draw is not there, drop it to the hitch and let him make a man miss.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
plays.whenToUse: The answer when they will not spread out with you. If they stay tight, the bubble has numbers. If they walk out to take it away, the quarterback runs into an empty box.

plays.name: QB Blast

reads.label: Count the Box
reads.text: Call it when the safeties are back and they are staying spread to match the wide splits. Four defenders in the box against five linemen and the quarterback is six on four.

reads.label: Straight Downhill
reads.text: There is no draw here. The line fires off, you get a double team on each side and the center climbs to the second level to pick up the safety. Twelve or thirteen before anybody touches you.

reads.label: Five in the Box Still Works
reads.text: Five in the box is five blockers plus the quarterback, so you still have the advantage. Hat on a hat, a guard gets up to the user, make one man miss.

reads.label: On the Goal Line
reads.text: A really good goal line and red zone run. If they are staying spread down there you already know it is a hat on a hat, and you are in.

adjustments: No adjustments needed
plays.whenToUse: The run for when they respect the splits and stay spread out. RPO Bubble QB Draw is the one for when they do not, because then you can hit the bubble and still have the quarterback run.

plays.name: All Go

reads.label: The Seam Against Single High
reads.text: Look at the safeties first. Single high and zone, go to the slot seam right away. The splits are so wide that the safety cannot get over, the corner is pulled out, and the deep crosser holds the linebacker inside. Fire it up the seam.

reads.label: The Seam Against Two High
reads.text: The seam has an inside stem to it. If the linebackers stay down on the crosser and there is no deep middle dropper, the outside streak holds the safety out there and you throw the seam as it stems up in front of him.

reads.label: The Deep Crosser
reads.text: If the linebackers stay shallow, throw the crosser as it gets in behind them. The jerk route helps pull them down. Or wait until he clears in behind the flat defender on the short side of the field.

reads.label: The Jerk Route
reads.text: The slot on the short side shoots out, then breaks back in over the middle. Against soft zone with everybody under the verticals he is the checkdown. Against man he gets really nice separation, and he is the best route on the play.

reads.label: The One on One Shot
reads.text: If they roll up and press the outside, or you get a matchup with a speed advantage and he has a step, do not be afraid to let it rip to one of the outside streaks. That is always part of four verticals.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
No other setup: get to the line and snap it
plays.whenToUse: A quick snap play that shows why the wide splits work. Read the safeties: single high is the seam, two high is the seam bending in front of the safety or the crosser, and the jerk route is the answer to man.

plays.name: Shock

reads.label: The Option Route
reads.text: The go to route. These option stick routes are super underrated against man: he puts his foot in the ground and breaks outside with two or three yards of separation. Fourth and six, rack catch, fifteen yards.

reads.label: The Stack Against Press
reads.text: When they press, motion the short side receiver in and you have a stack. The corner route gets a free release and makes a natural pick for the slant. The slant came completely free across his face for a touchdown, and the corner broke outside for a big gain.

reads.label: Against Off Coverage
reads.text: Leave him where he is. Now it is the slant breaking in with the skinny post behind it, and you go to whichever one has better separation. If the safety bites down on the slant, fire the post in over the top.

reads.label: The Comeback
reads.text: If the crossers are not getting open, wait for the comeback on the wide side to come back toward the football.

reads.label: The Shallow Cross
reads.text: The late option. The outside receiver on the wide side comes all the way across the field, so if you need something late, wait until he clears into the middle.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Outside receiver on the wide side on a shallow cross
Middle slot receiver on a comeback
Against press man: motion the outside receiver on the short side in to make a stack, then put him on a corner route
plays.whenToUse: The go to man beater out of five wide. The option route wins by itself, and when they press you build the stack on the short side and they cannot stay with either route.

plays.name: Deep Choice Drag

reads.label: The Slot Sits Against Zone
reads.text: The slot option is what makes it a veer and shoot play. Against Cover 3, Cover 2 or a Cover 2 invert he goes up the field and sits down in the zone. The corner is out, the linebackers get pulled inside, drop it in.

reads.label: The Dig Against Quarters and Palms
reads.text: Against Cover 4 he is one on one with the safety, so he does not sit in front of him and get jumped. He keeps going across the field on a dig. Three vertical stems on one side attack the leverage of the match players.

reads.label: The Deep Cross
reads.text: If the linebackers stay shallow and you do not like the sit, come to the crosser clearing in behind the flat defenders. Throw it between the hash and the numbers, or earlier between the hashes when they mug the gaps and you see pressure.

reads.label: The Post
reads.text: The third vertical on that side. Against Cover 3, against Quarters, and against Cover 2 it splits the safeties when there is no deep middle dropper.

reads.label: The Drag
reads.text: If they all drop way back under everything at the snap, the drag from the short side comes underneath as the checkdown.

adjustments: Trips to the wide side of the field
Outside receiver on the short side on a streak
Outside receiver on the wide side on a post
plays.whenToUse: The third choice route out of five wide. The slot sits against zone and runs the dig against Quarters and Palms, which makes it one of the better calls against the match coverage everybody is running.

plays.name: Stack QB Zone

reads.label: Count the Box
reads.text: The back is out in the stack, so three defenders leave the box to one side and three to the other, with a safety back. Now it is a really low number count in the middle of the field, and you do not have to worry about any of the wide defenders unless you bounce it.

reads.label: Run to the Tight End
reads.text: Usually run it to the tight end side. Good blocks at the point of attack and one man to beat. A little hurdle and you are in the end zone.

reads.label: The Cutback
reads.text: Press the gap, and if there is a cutback lane, put your foot in the ground and take it back the other way.

adjustments: No adjustments needed: come out in another play and audible to it when you like the box
plays.whenToUse: The run out of the stack. It looks just like Stack HB Screen and Stack Fk Screen Cross, so come out in one of those, and if you do not like the look, audible over and run it into the empty box.

plays.name: ISO Y Insert

reads.label: A Same Side Run
reads.text: Most shotgun runs go across the quarterback, away from where the back starts. This one stays on his side, where the tight end already is, so he gets downhill right away.

reads.label: Count His Side of the Center
reads.text: Count the defenders on the play side of the center. If they have three and we have three blockers plus the back, that is four on three. You see that a lot when you run play side with the tight end starting there.

reads.label: No Wasted Movement
reads.text: A quick downhill run. No searching for the hole, just hit it hard. Everybody gets collapsed outside or pinned in and it is a walk in on the goal line.

reads.label: Even Better Against Two High
reads.text: Two safeties back and it is two defenders against three blockers and the back. They are outnumbered at the point of attack.

adjustments: No adjustments needed
plays.whenToUse: The downhill run out of the stack formation, where most of the runs are quarterback runs. Count the tight end side, and if you have the extra body, hand it off and go.

plays.name: X Replace

reads.label: The Tight End Seam
reads.text: Your eyes go to the tight end right away. The splits create so much room up the seam that he is a cheat code even lined up tight. Against single high, just make sure the flat defender and the linebacker let him travel up the seam, and drop it in.

reads.label: Against Two High
reads.text: Even with a deep middle dropper back there, he bends in front of the safety. As long as the linebacker is not getting depth, throw it. Cover 2 or Cover 3, it is nasty.

reads.label: The Curl Against Man
reads.text: Man and match can take the seam away. Your eyes are already on that side, so if the tight end is capped, throw the curl as he sits down.

reads.label: The Mesh
reads.text: The back on the out and the receiver on the drag cross in the middle of the field. Against man, the back gets separation for the first down. Against Cover 3 match, the drag comes open on second and three.

reads.label: The Dig
reads.text: Whenever you have a mesh you want something deeper coming late. If the linebackers stay shallow on the two crossers, the dig comes in behind them.

adjustments: Stack to the wide side of the field
Back of the stack receiver on a drag (or the short in cut)
Running back on an out route to the wide side
Optional: outside receiver on the short side, stem his curl up one notch
plays.whenToUse: The tight end seam first, every time. When man or match caps it, the curl is on the same side, the mesh is underneath, and the dig comes in late behind the linebackers.

plays.name: HB CTR Strong

reads.label: Run It Against Two High
reads.text: This is the downhill run out of the swing formation, and you want it when both safeties are back.

reads.label: Count the Tight End Side
reads.text: It runs to the tight end, away from the back. Count that side of the center: three defenders against three blockers, and then the guard pulls, so it is four on three plus the back.

reads.label: Hat on a Hat
reads.text: Everybody is taken. The receiver gets a nice block, the puller seals it, and the hole is huge. Put your foot down for an easy ten to fifteen.

reads.label: On the Goal Line
reads.text: Everybody gets peeled inside and there is a huge gap. Untouched into the end zone.

adjustments: No adjustments needed
plays.whenToUse: Not a same side run like the iso, but it gets to the same place: a numbers advantage. The pulling guard gives you four on three to the tight end side when they sit in two high.

plays.name: PA Y Pop

reads.label: The Motioned Seam
reads.text: Absolutely nasty. The play fake looks like HB CTR Strong and the iso runs, so the linebackers get pulled down, and the wide splits leave the middle of the field empty. Against two high the safeties are too wide, and it was a forty seven yard walk in.

reads.label: Against Single High
reads.text: The same thing. You are just making sure the linebackers do not run with it. Even when it was his man in Cover 3 match, he bit on the fake and it was a thirty yard touchdown up the seam.

reads.label: The Corner on the Wide Side
reads.text: If a linebacker takes the seam away, the corner is on the wide side behind the clear out. If the flat defender stays shallow, throw it up the sideline. It is a good option against man as he breaks outside.

reads.label: The Drag
reads.text: Against man, buy a little time and the drag comes open as the checkdown. Against zone with everybody dropping way back, it is underneath.

adjustments: H-back to the wide side of the field, then motion him across
Outside receiver on the wide side on a streak
Backside solo receiver on a drag
plays.whenToUse: The shot off the run game. You can throw the motioned seam almost every time you call it, and the corner and the drag are there for the snaps when a linebacker finally runs with him.
